steps.body: Writing an equation means making a TRUE claim: choose values, join them, and make sure both sides really name the same value.
steps.narration: Writing an equation means making a TRUE claim: choose values, join them, and make sure both sides really name the same value.

widget.prompt: Write-and-check: your equation says 6 + 3 = 9. Verify it — start at 6 and count on 3. Where do you land?
widget.missFeedback: Start at 6 and count on 3: you land on 9.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 9 — your written claim holds, so it is a true equation worth keeping.

predict.prompt: You write an equation of your own. What must you do before trusting it?
predict.reveal: A written claim is only an equation once its sides are verified to match.

widget.prompt: You want to write your own TRUE equation. Which one works?

options.feedback: Correct — this statement is true because both sides have the value 12.
A written equation must be TRUE; the left side is 12, not 14.
Without an equals sign this is an expression, not an equation.
An equals sign between two different values makes a false statement, not a usable equation.
